## 1 Abstract

[`mhp_app()`](https://myaseen208.com/mhpfilter/reference/mhp_app.md)
opens an application in the web browser that runs the filters of the
package without code: the data, the HP, modified HP and fully modified
HP filters, their comparison, the diagnostics of the end-point bias,
many series at once and the simulation study. This vignette describes
its pages and how it keeps its results reproducible.

## 2 Starting the application

``` r

mhp_app(
    launch.browser = TRUE
  )
```

The application needs the suggested packages **shiny**, **bslib** and
**DT**. **magick** with WebP support is optional: with it the plots are
sent to the browser as WebP images, smaller than the same PNG.

## 3 The pages

| Page | What it does |
|----|----|
| Home | what the application does and the order of the pages |
| Data | the `us_macro` example or a CSV file with one series per column; the series, its frequency and first period, and whether to filter its logarithm |
| Filter | the fully modified HP, modified HP or HP filter with its settings; interpretation, plot, table, printed output and R code |
| Compare | the three filters on the same series: moments of the cycles, the end-point loss and the spread of the cycle at the ends and in the middle |
| Diagnostics | the end-point loss, the gain functions or the filter weights for the smoothing parameters of the last fit |
| Batch | every numeric column of the data, each with its own smoothing parameter |
| Simulation | the power comparison of Hanif et al. (2017) for chosen designs |
| References | the articles behind the methods, as [`mhp_cite()`](https://myaseen208.com/mhpfilter/reference/mhp_cite.md) prints them |

Every result page has the same tabs:

- **Interpretation** gives the plain-language reading of
  [`mhp_interpret()`](https://myaseen208.com/mhpfilter/reference/mhp_interpret.md),
  with a button that copies it.
- **Plot** shows the figure, which can be saved as PNG, PDF or WebP.
- **Table** shows the numbers, rounded, in a sortable table with buttons
  to copy them or save them as CSV or Excel.
- **Output** shows the printed result as text, with a button that copies
  it.

The filter page has a further tab, **R code**, with the code that
reproduces the fit outside the application.

The loss on the diagnostics page (0.79) is larger than the loss in the
interpretation (0.62): the procedure chooses the weights by their loss
at \\\lambda\\ of the modified HP filter (683) and then searches
\\\lambda\\ again (1448), and the loss is reported at the first, as in
the MATLAB code. The diagnostics page evaluates it at the second.

## 4 Reproducibility

For the settings of the screenshots, the R code tab shows:

``` r

settings <-
  list(
      source       = "example"
    , freq         = "4"
    , col          = "gdp"
    , start        = 1959
    , start_period = 1
    , logs         = TRUE
    , method       = "fmhp"
    , max_lambda   = 3000
    , k_linear     = 15
    , k_quadratic  = NA
    , schemes      = c("linear", "quadratic")
    , form         = "rows"
    )
cat(mhpfilter:::.mhp_app_code(input = settings))
```

    library(mhpfilter)
    data(us_macro)
    dat <- us_macro
    x <- ts(dat$gdp, start = c(1959, 1), frequency = 4)
    fit <-
      fmhp_filter(
          x               = x
        , max_lambda      = 3000
        , k_linear        = 15
        , k_quadratic     = NULL
        , alpha_linear    = seq(from = 0, to = 2000, by = 10)
        , alpha_quadratic = seq(from = 0, to = 2000, by = 5)
        , schemes         = c("linear", "quadratic")
        , form            = "rows"
        , lambda          = NULL
        , log_scale       = TRUE
        , as_dt           = FALSE
        )
    fit
    plot(x = fit)
    mhp_interpret(
        x   = fit
      , top = 3
      )

The filters are deterministic, so the code returns the same numbers as
the application.

## 5 Deploying

[`mhp_app_object()`](https://myaseen208.com/mhpfilter/reference/mhp_app.md)
returns the application object without running it, for a server:

``` r

# app.R on a Shiny server
mhpfilter::mhp_app_object()
```
